stem: In the management of Stevens-Johnson syndrome, what is the purpose of 'sweeping' the fornices with a glass rod?

options.text: To prevent the mucous membranes from sticking together and forming symblepharon.
To collect epithelial cells for PCR testing and diagnosis confirmation.
To apply topical acyclovir ointment deep into the upper eyelid.
To remove alkali particles that have become embedded in the conjunctiva.

explanation: During healing, the conjunctival surfaces can adhere to each other; sweeping prevents these adhesions (symblepharon) which lead to dry eye and scarring.
rationale: This procedure is done to stop different parts of the eye's lining from fusing together during healing.

optionExplanations.A: During healing, the conjunctival surfaces can adhere to each other; sweeping prevents these adhesions (symblepharon) which lead to dry eye and scarring.
optionExplanations.B: Diagnosis is usually clinical based on systemic symptoms; the glass rod is a therapeutic tool to prevent adhesions, not a diagnostic one.
optionExplanations.C: Acyclovir is used for HSV; Stevens-Johnson syndrome requires lubricants and prevention of mechanical adhesions.
optionExplanations.D: Particle removal is part of chemical burn management, whereas the glass rod in Stevens-Johnson is for preventing tissue fusion.
